en: Petavatthu,
Cūḷavagga 3.
The Story of the Wheelwright’s Ghost (Rathakārapetivatthu)
“Having ascended a celestial mansion made of radiant,
beautiful beryl pillars and adorned with many colors,
you dwell there, O goddess of great majesty.”
On the fifteenth day of the waxing moon, the moon is at its fullness.
Your complexion is like refined gold,
brilliantly radiant and most beautiful to behold.
Seated upon this incomparable, supreme couch, you are all alone; there is no husband for you.
And these lotus ponds surround you on every side.
Abounding with many garlands and numerous white lotuses,
strewn all around with golden dust,
there is neither mud nor moss to be found there.
These swans are beautiful and delightful;
they always move about upon the water.
Having gathered together, they all cry out in sweet harmony.
The sound of Bindusara is like the roar of kettledrums.
Resplendent with glory,
O glorious one, you stand leaning upon the ship.
O lady with long, curling eyelashes, smiling and speaking sweetly,
you who are beautiful in every limb, you shine forth brilliantly.
This stainless celestial mansion stands firm and level.
“O woman, I desire to rejoice here with you in the Nandana grove of Anomadassi,
which possesses gardens and increases delight and joy.”
“Perform an action here that will be experienced in this life,
and let your mind be fixed upon this very life;
having performed an action here that will be experienced in this life,”
"In this way you shall obtain me, you who desire love.
Having promised her "So be it," he performed there the deed to be experienced [in that state].
Having performed an action there to be experienced [in that state],
that young man was reborn into her companionship.
Thus ends the third story, the Story of the Cartwright Peta.
The second section for recitation.
